**Síncope** é uma nota que começa num te: **Syncopation** is a note that starts on a weak beat (or on the offbeat) and carries over the strong beat. Your ear expects the accent on 1 and it arrives *early*. It's the basis of samba, funk, reggae and MPB.
A forma mais comum é a **antecipação**:: The most common form is **anticipation**: the note that should fall on 1 arrives half an eighth early, on the *and* of 4, tied into the next bar.
Colcheia, semínima, semínima, semínima p: Eighth, quarter, quarter, dotted quarter: the notes fall on the *ands*.
Bata o pé no tempo. As notas sincopadas: Tap your foot on the beat. The syncopated notes fall with your foot **in the air**.

Treino clássico do jazz e do funk: o met: A classic jazz and funk drill: the metronome plays **only the offbeats**. You keep counting *1 and 2 and*, but the click falls on the *and*.
No metrônomo abaixo, escolha o modo **co: In the metronome below, choose the **offbeats** mode. At first it feels like the click *flipped*. Keep at it until it sounds like the right place.

No **6/8** cabem 6 colcheias por compass: In **6/8** there are 6 eighth notes per bar, grouped as **2 groups of 3**: **ONE** two three **FOUR** five six. Your foot taps twice per bar (on 1 and 4).
É o balanço das baladas *soul*, das canç: It's the sway of *soul* ballads, lullabies and a lot of folk music.
Toque baixo no 1 e no 4, e as cordas agu: Play the bass on 1 and 4, and the high strings on the other eighth notes. The BPM here counts **eighth notes**.
**12/8** = quatro grupos de três colchei: **12/8** = four groups of three eighth notes. Each beat divides into **three**: *ONE-and-a TWO-and-a…* (triplets).
O **shuffle** do mês 4 é o 12/8 com a no: Month 4's **shuffle** is 12/8 with the middle note of each group silent: *DOO - ba, DOO - ba*. That's why shuffle and slow blues go together so well.
Num blues lento, cada nota pesa. Toque m: In a slow blues, every note weighs. Play less and let it ring.
No jazz, as colcheias são suingadas (lon: In jazz, eighth notes are swung (long-short), but lighter and accented on the **offbeat**. The drummer marks **2 and 4** on the hi-hat.
A guitarra base faz o **Charleston**: ac: The rhythm guitar plays the **Charleston**: a short chord on **1** and on the **and of 2**. Simple, and it leaves room for the rest of the band.
No reggae, a guitarra toca **só nos cont: In reggae, the guitar plays **only on the offbeats** (2 and 4, or on the *ands*), with very short chords on the high strings. Beat 1 belongs to the bass and drums.

A bossa nasceu no violão de dedo: o **po: Bossa nova was born on fingerstyle nylon guitar: the **thumb** plays the bass on **1 and 3** (root and fifth), and the **fingers** play the chord on syncopated spots that change from bar to bar. On guitar with a pick, simplify: bass on the beat, chord on the pattern's spots.
A levada se repete a cada **dois compass: The pattern repeats every **two bars** and is related to the Cuban **clave**. That's why bossa always seems to be *floating*.
A bossa raramente usa tríades. Os acorde: Bossa rarely uses triads. Chords get **9ths**, **6ths** and **13ths**: notes that don't change the function, only the color.
Progressão clássica de bossa (original d: A classic bossa progression (Pauta original, in the style): **Dm9 – G13 – Cmaj9 – A7b9**.
O samba é escrito em **2/4**, com semico: Samba is written in **2/4**, with sixteenth notes. The strong accent is on the **second beat** (the surdo drum). On guitar, the right hand plays continuous sixteenths, hitting only some of them: the pattern below is a simplified version of the cavaquinho and guitar *teleco-teco*.
Comece a 70 BPM. Samba de verdade costum: Start at 70 BPM. Real samba usually goes past 100.

O baião se apoia numa célula de três not: Baião rests on a three-note cell every two beats: **dotted eighth, sixteenth, eighth** (*BOOM - ba BOOM*). It's the rhythm of the zabumba drum.
O **xote** é mais lento e dançado *dois: **Xote** is slower and danced *two steps this way, two steps that way*, with a muted strum on the offbeat:
Muitas melodias de baião usam a **escala: Many baião melodies use the **Mixolydian scale** (major with a minor 7th). You'll study it in month 9; for now, notice the sound of **G7** as the main chord.

A **3ª** diz se o acorde é maior ou meno: The **3rd** says whether the chord is major or minor. The **7th** says whether it's maj7, m7 or 7. Together they're the **guide tones**: play just those two and your ear already understands the harmony. The bass takes care of the root; the 5th barely changes anything.
Cmaj7: as notas-guia estão a poucas casa: Cmaj7: the guide tones are just a few frets from each other.
Repare: entre Dm7 e G7 só **uma nota** s: Notice: between Dm7 and G7 only **one note** moves (C → B). Between G7 and Cmaj7, just one (F → E). The harmony moves by **half steps**.

Separando as duas vozes, saem duas **lin: Separating the two voices gives you two **lines**: one goes down from C to B (7 → 3 → 7) and the other from F to E (3 → 7 → 3). A good solo melody often follows one of these lines underneath the fast notes.

**Vibrato** é balançar a altura da nota,: **Vibrato** is wobbling the note's pitch, going up and back quickly. It's what makes a long note *alive*, like a voice.
**Rock e blues:** gire o **punho** como: **Rock and blues:** rotate your **wrist** like a bend, in small repeated bends. Use the support fingers.
**Jazz e clássico:** mova o dedo **ao lo: **Jazz and classical:** move your finger **along** the string (sideways), a narrower vibrato.
Controle duas coisas: **largura** (quant: Control two things: **width** (how far it goes up) and **speed**. Practice slow and wide, then fast and narrow.
Toque **uma nota por compasso**, só nota: Play **one note per bar**, pentatonic notes only, each with vibrato. It seems like little, but it's one of the most musical exercises there is.
Vibrato não é tremer a mão. Se o braço i: Vibrato isn't shaking your hand. If your whole arm shakes, slow down.
**Ataque:** palheta mais perto do braço: **Attack:** picking closer to the neck = soft; near the bridge = bright and aggressive.

No blues, cada acorde é um 7, com sua pr: In the blues, every chord is a 7, with its own 3rd and 7th: **A7 (C#, G)**, **D7 (F#, C)**, **E7 (G#, D)**. The A minor pentatonic has G, C and D, but **not** C#, F# or G#. That's why the blues greats mix: pentatonic for color, guide tones for harmony.
